title: Breadcrumbs for hierarchical location
summary: Use breadcrumbs to show a user's location inside a meaningful hierarchy and provide direct access to ancestor levels.
problem: Deep hierarchical products become difficult to navigate when users can only move with browser back or a global menu.
use_when: Content or objects have stable parent-child hierarchy
Users may enter deep pages directly from search, links, or notifications
avoid_when: The product is shallow or sequence-based rather than hierarchical
The breadcrumb would repeat a single obvious parent
rationale: Breadcrumbs communicate both location and escape routes.
They complement rather than replace primary navigation.

prefer_alternatives_if: The relationship between pages is a linear workflow rather than a hierarchy
use_if: Content or objects have stable parent-child hierarchy
Users may enter deep pages directly from search, links, or notifications

requirements: Use navigational semantics and a descriptive label for the breadcrumb region.
Mark the current page without making it a misleading link.
Show ancestors in order from broad to specific.
Avoid truncation that removes the only differentiating text.
